title: shellcheck
same: Every counted sample's results were read from its own job logs. In all 30 counted samples (15 cold, 15 warm) the same 14 checks ran and passed: the test suite under each of six GHC versions (8.0, 8.10, 9.0.1, 9.4.7, 9.6.6 and latest), the release binary for each of seven targets (linux x86_64, aarch64, armv6hf and riscv64, darwin x86_64 and aarch64, windows x86_64), and the release package. Each test suite ran the same 2438 QuickCheck properties, all passing, in every sample; the source package, every binary, its upload and (except the two darwin binaries, which are cross-built and cannot run here) its `--version` smoke check, and every package were present in every sample. The binaries were not compared byte for byte: with the agent PR the `linux.armv6hf` binary is built incrementally, so its build id, version stamp and a few hundred bytes of address fields differ from a clean build.
notes: **Workflows in this merge.** The replayed merge runs `build.yml` (package the source, test under six GHC versions, build seven targets, package the binaries). Upstream's other workflow, `distrotest.yaml`, runs only on a release, a schedule or a manual dispatch, so it does not run here. The ARM, macOS, Windows and RISC-V binaries are cross-built inside Docker on the x64 Linux runners, so no job runs on other hardware; the `linux.armv6hf` build runs in an emulated (qemu) chroot in every configuration.

**Lanes.** Samples ran concurrently, each in its own cache scope (one repository per lane, with the same branches, events and payloads); 21 samples came from an earlier sequential run of the same configuration. The other 9 samples, all warm, ran in the lanes: GitHub-hosted runners rounds 4 and 5, StarSling Runners (with agents) rounds 2 to 5, and 3 samples of the agent PR's own check. Their runs are linked in the sample table.

**Bench-only changes, identical in every configuration and never part of the agent PR:**
  - Switched off: the `Deploy binaries` job (GitHub release upload, Docker Hub push and a 300-second sleep). Upstream's own condition is kept with `false &&` in front. Its secrets do not exist here and nothing may be published. Upstream's run did execute this job, including the 5-minute sleep, so that upstream work is not in any column, and these waits are shorter than upstream's own run by design.
  - The three secret references (`DOCKER_USERNAME`, `DOCKER_PASSWORD`, `DOCKER_EMAIL`) are removed; only the switched-off job reads them.
  - Version string: `setgitversion` runs `git describe`, which is changed to `git describe --tags --always` so it cannot fail when no tag is found. It changes only the version text.
  - Runner labels: upstream's `ubuntu-latest` is replaced by the runner label of each configuration (see Runner sizes).
  - One harness step, `Benchmark event context (harness)`, is added at the start of every job. It prints two IDs so each job can be matched to its sample; its median time is 0 s.
  - On the agent PR's own branch (`starsling/develop`) only, a setup commit points the workflow's triggers at that branch and its runners at StarSling, so the PR's checks run there. The measured replays do not use it.

**Caches and the warm seed.** Before each warm sample, a seed run replays the previous upstream merge ([`2c5668ba`](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/commit/2c5668bac4dabd53afe57b4faa60b7054cd064bb), onto `5d6a0bb1`, which changes `src/ShellCheck/Analytics.hs`) on the same configuration and the same branch, so the sample can read the cache it saves; its time is not counted. Upstream's own tests failed on that merge (upstream run [42545272915](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/actions/runs/42545272915)); every seed run used here passed. In every warm sample with the agent PR, the `linux.armv6hf` build restored the build cache saved for the seed's merge.

**Root and non-root StarSling jobs.** StarSling switched jobs from root to an ordinary user at about 11:13 AM PST (19:13 UTC) on 2026-11-16. Samples are classed by their first workflow start. As root: all 10 cold StarSling samples and warm round 1 of StarSling Runners (with agents) (plus warm rounds 1 and 2 of the agent PR's own check). As an ordinary user: warm rounds 2 to 5 of StarSling Runners (with agents) (plus warm rounds 3 to 5 of the agent PR's own check). The owner accepted mixing the two; a check before pooling found no shift: the agent PR's build step took 83 s in the one warm root sample and 78 to 86 s in the four ordinary-user ones.

**Replaced samples.** One sample that never finished was discarded and re-run: the StarSling Runners (with agents) sample of cold round 1; it left no record. The experiment was reopened (the reopening is recorded in the experiment record) and the sample re-run from a fresh cold cache. Separately, StarSling samples count only when every StarSling runner used a RAM disk for storage. Four warm StarSling samples ran after a StarSling storage change on runners that used disk storage or whose storage could not be confirmed; they were voided and re-run in the lanes: StarSling Runners (with agents) rounds 2 and 3, and rounds 3 and 4 of the agent PR's own check. In every counted sample, no job waited more than 27 s for a runner.

**Runner sizes.** Upstream's `ubuntu-latest` jobs run on GitHub `ubuntu-26.04-4core` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB) and StarSling `starsling-ubuntu-26.04` (4 vCPU, 16 GiB). StarSling's 4 vCPU runners can burst to 5 vCPU and 32 GB RAM (Afterburner); GitHub's 4-core runners have 16 GB. Every job in this merge runs on those labels.

**Upstream reference (context only; not like-for-like; not the headline).** What upstream sees today: a median 34.8 min per merge to the default branch on upstream's own GitHub runners (n=12, most recent comparable merges to the default branch within the last 60 days; standard runners, warm caches, many commits; not a like-for-like replay).
**Failed or re-run samples** (replaced, not in the medians): GitHub-hosted runners: 0; StarSling Runners (with agents): 2; the agent PR's own check: 2.

agentPrs.summary: Cache the build directory of the `linux.armv6hf` build and build incrementally. Three files: the workflow restores a persistent `dist-newstyle` with `actions/cache`, the builder container mounts it, and `build.incremental` restores the old modification times of source files whose content is unchanged, so GHC 9.0 recompiles only the modules that changed. Adds one `sudo chown` step.

whatWasSlow: Every merge to ShellCheck's default branch runs one workflow, `build.yml`. After the source package, its 13 test and build jobs start together. All but one finish in a few minutes. The `linux.armv6hf` build does not: it builds ShellCheck with GHC 9.0 inside an emulated ARM chroot, from scratch each time, and nothing is cached between runs. That one job is almost the whole wait: in this benchmark, cold, it took a median 1893 s of the 2019 s merge on GitHub-hosted runners, and 1198 s of the 1292 s merge on StarSling Runners (with agents), where a cold run has nothing to restore. The next-longest jobs are the test suites, the longest of them GHC 8.0 at a median 495 s on GitHub-hosted runners and 334 s on StarSling Runners (with agents), cold.
whatWeChanged:
The original showcase for this project proposed one fix: keep the `linux.armv6hf` build directory between runs and compile only what changed. It was measured on its own on StarSling Runners, with 5 runs on each side (the CI as it was, and the CI with the fix), on the step it changes.

| Fix | Result | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| Cache the `linux.armv6hf` build directory and build incrementally | `linux.armv6hf` build step, warm: 1220 s to 88 s (median); every run with the fix beat every run without it. Cold (nothing to restore): 1191 s to 1183 s | Kept (agent PR 1) |

With the fix, the `linux.armv6hf` job takes a median 95 s warm, and the test suites become the longest jobs. The fix is a cache, so it only helps when a cache from an earlier merge exists, and only as far as that merge's changes are small. The replayed merge changes only the manual page (`shellcheck.1.md`), so on the warm runs no Haskell module had to be recompiled. A merge that changes Haskell modules recompiles those modules, and one that changes `ShellCheck.cabal`, the builder image or a core module (`AST`, `Interface`, `Prelude`) recompiles most of them and gains little.
